|errata_history=This is the original printed text of [[A Useless Gesture (V) (Virtual Set D)]] (version 1 of 4). The image here is the slip of the PC's Virtual Card Master Set (August 2016). The current text is [[A Useless Gesture (V) (Virtual Set D) (Errata 3)]] (PC-E3). Each version below is quoted in full with its dated source. Every publication that differs visibly from the one before is a version, numbered in release order; a printed errata mark that does not match that order is recorded as a PC transcription error (Bill, 11 and 12 November 2026).
* '''Original''' (this page): Slip in the PC's Virtual Card Master Set (Set 0), official text as of 1 August 2016<ref name="ms2016">Players Committee, Virtual Card Master Set (Set 0) PDF <code>Set-0.pdf</code>, “Official text as of August 1, 2016” (file created 2 August 2016), page 4, slip “•A Useless Gesture (V)” ([https://web.archive.org/web/20160806222234/http://www.starwarsccg.org/virtual/Set-0.pdf Internet Archive copy of 6 August 2016]).</ref>: “Plays on table. In order to play an Interrupt from Lost Pile, opponent must first stack it here (if possible) and use +1 Force for each card here, even if Interrupt is normally free. Revolution is canceled.” Printed: a partial slip (the “DEFENSIVE SHIELD” band and the game-text box only), to be laid over the Decipher card; lower-left name “•A Useless Gesture”; no errata mark. The PC first released this card with [[Virtual Set 0]] / [[Virtual Set D]] on 24 September 2014; the slips of that first release do not survive in the Internet Archive, so this sheet is the earliest surviving text.
* '''PC-E1''' ([[A Useless Gesture (V) (Virtual Set D) (Errata)]]): Slip in the PC's re-issued Virtual Card Master Set (Set 0) (file created 30 May 2017)<ref name="ms2017">The same PDF re-issued by the PC (file created 30 May 2017), page 2 ([https://web.archive.org/web/20170704234722/http://www.starwarsccg.org/virtual/Set-0.pdf Internet Archive copy of 4 July 2017]).</ref>: “Plays on table. In order to play an Interrupt from Lost Pile, opponent must first stack it here (if possible) and use +1 Force for each card here, even if Interrupt is normally free. Revolution is canceled.” Printed: a partial slip (the “DEFENSIVE SHIELD” band and the game-text box only), to be laid over the Decipher card; lower-left name “•A Useless Gesture”; no errata mark. '''Errata mark:''' this slip prints no errata mark but is errata 1 in release order; recorded as printed and listed as a [[Players Committee transcription errors|PC transcription error]] (Bill, 12 November 2026). '''What changed:''' Same words. The slip was re-drawn: the Interrupt icon moved from beside the game-text box up into the “DEFENSIVE SHIELD” band, and the game-text box was made larger. A visible change, so a version (Bill, 12 November 2026).
* '''PC-E2''' ([[A Useless Gesture (V) (Virtual Set D) (Errata 2)]]): Card image published 8 July 2018<ref name="v2-1">PC card image in the PC's Holotable image set: [https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/blob/022435b/Images-HT/starwars/ResetDS-Dark/large/auselessgesture.gif auselessgesture.gif], commit [https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/commit/022435b 022435b] (8 July 2018, “Set 9 load”).</ref>: “Plays on table. In order to play an Interrupt from Lost Pile, opponent must first stack it here (if possible) and use +1 Force for each card here, even if Interrupt is normally free. Revolution is canceled.” Printed: no errata mark; lower-left name “•A Useless Gesture”. The PC first released this shield with [[Virtual Set 0]] / [[Virtual Set D]] on 24 September 2014. The PC's Holotable image set starts on 8 July 2018, so this is the earliest surviving PC card image; whether the 2014 release slip had the same words is not shown by it. '''Errata mark:''' this image prints no errata mark but is errata 2 in release order; recorded as printed and listed as a [[Players Committee transcription errors|PC transcription error]] (Bill, 12 November 2026). '''What changed:''' Same words as the slip above. This is the first PC card image of the card (the PC's Holotable image set starts on 8 July 2018): the whole card is drawn, with frame, picture and icons, instead of a print-and-cut slip. A visibly different publication, so a version (Bill, 11 and 12 November 2026).
* '''PC-E3''' ([[A Useless Gesture (V) (Virtual Set D) (Errata 3)]]): Card image published 31 July 2022<ref name="v3-1">PC card image in the PC's Holotable image set: [https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/blob/ab74419/Images-HT/starwars/ResetDS-Dark/large/auselessgesture.gif auselessgesture.gif], commit [https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/commit/ab74419 ab74419] (31 July 2022, “updated hires gifs”); high-resolution image <code>ResetDS-Dark/hires/auselessgesture.png</code>, commit [https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/commit/594c3a0 594c3a0] (31 July 2022, “Set 0 Hi Res”).</ref>: “Plays on table. In order to play an Interrupt from Lost Pile, opponent must first stack it here (if possible) and use +1 Force for each card here, even if Interrupt is normally free. Revolution is canceled.” Printed: no errata mark; lower-left name “A Useless Gesture”. '''Errata mark:''' this image prints no errata mark but is errata 3 in release order; recorded as printed and listed as a [[Players Committee transcription errors|PC transcription error]] (Bill, 12 November 2026). '''What changed:''' re-rendered by the PC in its high-resolution card style (new frame, colours and typesetting); same words. The bullet is dropped from the lower-left name (“A Useless Gesture”). No errata mark.
|notes='''Blanked:''' The Players Committee cut this shield from Virtual Set D with [[Virtual Set 23]] on 22 July 2024: the July 2024 Defensive Shield Update Kit lists “•A Useless Gesture (V)” under “Dark Side – Cut”<ref name="dskit2024">Players Committee, [https://res.starwarsccg.org/virtual/DShieldUpdateKit_2024_July.pdf July 2024 Defensive Shield Update Kit] (PDF, 3 pages, “SWCCG Players Committee, July 2024”; file built 2 August 2024), released with [[Virtual Set 23]] (22 July 2024).</ref>. It was replaced by the new [[A Useless Gesture & •Death Star Sentry]] combo card. A blanked card is treated as if it did not exist from that date (in effect a ban); it is not a new version. It stays in its set and is legal in period formats that end before the blanking.
